review_contract.mechanism: There is NO dedicated snapshot-review function and NO role grant that reaches public.exercise_catalog (migration 023 section 11 REVOKEs ALL from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and grants nothing back on this table; the four migration-027 NOLOGIN roles hold EXECUTE on load/review/admit/publish CONTENT functions only). The lawful transition surface is therefore ONE direct privileged UPDATE, in the hosted operator context, that sets review_status AND the complete fresh audit tuple (reviewed_by, reviewed_at, review_rationale) in the SAME statement. The operative BEFORE trigger (exlib_freeze_catalog_snapshot, REPLACED by migration 027) validates the transition and ITSELF appends the immutable exercise_catalog_review_events row (which is why that events table's own guard accepts inserts only at trigger depth >= 2).
review_contract.allowed_transitions: pending -> approved | revised | rejected; approved -> revised | rejected; revised and rejected are TERMINAL; review_status can never return to pending; re-approval after a non-approved decision requires a NEW catalog version row.
review_contract.fresh_audit_tuple_rule: EVERY transition requires a complete, non-blank audit tuple, and the tuple must DIFFER from the row's prior tuple (a status-only flip or evidence reuse fails: 'a review transition must carry FRESH evidence'). Audit fields may never change except together with an allowed transition.
review_contract.governed_content_immutable: The snapshot's identity/content field set is IMMUTABLE (any change requires a new catalog version row): logical_id, canonical_name, category, primary_muscle, equipment, laterality, tracking_mode, source_url, source_page, retrieved_at, import_confidence, provenance, movement_pattern, training_role, difficulty, availability, catalog_version, created_at. The review decision therefore approves or refuses EXACTLY this frozen content; the transition writes ONLY review_status plus the audit tuple.
review_contract.seal_scope: Sealing a delivery run validates ONLY that run's MEMBERS (every exercise member must be approved, active, and fully review-audited, and membership must be non-empty); snapshots outside the run's membership do not block sealing.
review_contract.one_use: One-way status machine plus the fresh-tuple rule: each transition happens at most once per (from,to) pair per row, every transition is appended forever to exercise_catalog_review_events, and deactivation/reactivation can never relaunder a decision (reactivation is forbidden outright).

proposed_transition.on_APPROVE: approved (one direct privileged UPDATE carrying a complete fresh audit tuple; the trigger appends the immutable review event)
proposed_transition.on_REJECT: rejected (TERMINAL; delivering this content would then require a NEW catalog version row and a new review)
proposed_transition.on_CORRECT: revised (TERMINAL for this row; the correction itself requires a NEW catalog version row carrying the corrected content, then its own review)

prior_decisions_not_reused: The EXLIB-2I human decision (applied hosted by EXLIB-2P) reviewed the exercise_catalog_content row (content_status), a DIFFERENT reviewed-object class: the 2I record itself states the decision involved no catalog snapshot, and the 2P record shows the applied fields were content_status/reviewed_by/reviewed_at/review_rationale on the CONTENT row while the snapshot stayed pending with NULL reviewer fields. Classification: NOT REUSABLE for this snapshot review; a new snapshot-scoped human decision is required (this form).
no_effect_statement: This form grants no approval and has no mechanical effect. Blank or null NEVER reads as approval. Even a filled, approved form changes nothing by itself: applying the decision to the hosted row is a later, separately prepared, separately reviewed, one-use application package executed by Joseph/ChatGPT - never by Claude.
preparer_boundary: Claude and ChatGPT may prepare and validate this form but may NEVER fill or fabricate the human fields (decision, reviewer, reviewer_role_or_credential, reviewed_at, rationale, evidence). A fabricated or preselected value voids the form.

lifecycle.state: PREPARED_BLANK_TEMPLATE - this prepared blank form is an approved template, NOT a decision; blank or null NEVER reads as approval
lifecycle.lawful_completion_transition: EXACTLY ONE lawful transition exists: a HUMAN changes the six human_fields (decision, reviewer, reviewer_role_or_credential, reviewed_at, rationale, evidence) from null to complete human-supplied values. NO field may remain null in a completed decision (if the reviewer supplies no optional evidence, the reviewer personally records an explicit no-evidence statement - never the preparer). NO machine or preparer may fill or preselect any of them, and NO OTHER BYTE of the form may change in that transition.
lifecycle.post_completion_immutability: AFTER human completion, any further byte change to the completed form voids the decision.
lifecycle.external_voiding: Independently of completion state, any change to the promoted source files fingerprinted below, or to the hosted row state this form describes (a review event appearing, the row deactivating, or any governed field differing at application time), voids the decision; the application package must re-verify all of it fail-closed before applying anything.
lifecycle.no_database_effect: Filling the form has NO database effect. Applying the completed decision to the hosted row remains a separately prepared, separately reviewed, one-use application package executed by Joseph/ChatGPT - never by Claude.
